texts: bad: two over-claims — the parse invents a kind called 'neighboring station' rather than recording ordinary stations that happen to neighbor the Cove, and it asserts outright that wraith activity exists at the Sunken Cove, which your sentence only supposes. Use the explicit recurrence word and move the descriptor out of the noun phrase: 'Whenever wraith activity at the Sunken Cove increases, the stations near the Sunken Cove request feather rations from the Council.' Your 'Whenever wraith sightings ... rise' version parsed with no such standing claim, so that is the shape to copy.
good. a fireable per-occasion rule with the Council as the party asked and the rations recorded as what is asked for; the reviewer's one flag was overruled on adjudication.
good. every participant is covered — the Council, the requests, and the central feather store the weighing is done against.

bad: the parse over-commits twice — it records the drained lanterns as component parts of the stations, where your 'with' says only that the stations have them, and it files the rule as an absolute universal rather than the general tendency a bare plural states. Make the relation an explicit verb: 'The Council prioritizes stations that have drained lanterns.' If you do mean every such station without exception, write 'every station with drained lanterns' so the strength is read off an actual quantifier word.
